listenings.text: Almost every adult learner I coach hits the same wall around the middle of a program. In the first months, progress is fast and easy to see. You learn the words for your job, and every week you can do something new. Then, around the halfway point, it feels like nothing is changing. That's normal. It's the learning curve getting flatter, not you getting worse. Here's what I tell people. First, stop measuring words, and start measuring situations. Can you run a meeting? Can you disagree politely? Those are the real numbers. Second, choose three focus areas, not ten. And third, record yourself today, and keep the file. In six months, you'll listen to it, and you'll hear the difference.

When I moved to Frankfurt for my bank, my English was good on paper, but in meetings I used to stay quiet. I used to wait until I had the perfect sentence, and by then the conversation had moved on. The turning point was a project review. My director asked me why I never pushed back, and honestly, it was a wake-up call. Since then, I've changed two things. I've stopped waiting for the perfect sentence, and I've started using a few simple phrases I can always fall back on, like, let me put that in context. My English isn't perfect today, but I've become much more visible in the room. And that has changed my career more than any grammar book.
